"'''Got My Mind Set on You'''" (also written as "'''(Got My Mind) Set on You'''") is a song written and composed by [[Rudy Clark]] and originally recorded by [[James Ray (singer)|James Ray]] in 1962, under the title "'''I've Got My Mind Set on You'''". An edited version of the song was released later in the year as a single on Dynamic Sound Records credited to Ray with [[Hutch Davie]] Orchestra & Chorus. The song features a variety of instruments, including a [[Pipa|Chinese lute]], but it is uncertain whether Ray or the orchestra played the lute.
In 1987, [[George Harrison]] released a [[cover version]] of the song on his eleventh studio album ''[[Cloud Nine (George Harrison album)|Cloud Nine]]'', which he had recorded on his [[Dark Horse Records]] label.

"Got My Mind Set on You" (also written as "(Got My Mind) Set on You") is a song written and composed by Rudy Clark and originally recorded by James Ray in 1962, under the title "I've Got My Mind Set on You". An edited version of the song was released later in the year as a single on Dynamic Sound Records credited to Ray with Hutch Davie Orchestra & Chorus. The song features a variety of instruments, including a Chinese lute, but it is uncertain whether Ray or the orchestra played the lute.
In 1987, George Harrison released a cover version of the song on his eleventh studio album Cloud Nine, which he had recorded on his Dark Horse Records label.

While there, Harrison visited record shops and bought a variety of albums. One was Ray's 1962 album that contained the song "I've Got My Mind Set on You". In January 1987, Harrison began recording the song at his [[Friar Park]] home studio, with [[Jeff Lynne]] producing and playing bass and keyboards, [[Jim Keltner]] on drums, [[Jim Horn]] on sax, and [[Ray Cooper]] on percussion.Womack, Kenneth. [https://www.salon.com/2020/02/24/george-harrison-beatles-got-my-mind-set-on-you/ "How George Harrison made his last number 1 hit, 'Got My Mind Set On You'"]. ''Salon''. February 24, 2020. It was released on October 12, 1987, in the US. Of Harrison's three number-one singles in the US, it was the only song not written or composed by Harrison himself. Not only was it the last US number-one hit by Harrison but, {{As of|2026|lc=y}}, the last time a former Beatle hit number one in either the US or UK as a solo artist. When the song hit number one, it broke a three-way tie between Harrison, [[John Lennon]], and [[Ringo Starr]], all of whom had two number-one hit singles as solo artists in the US ([[Paul McCartney]] had three solo number-one singles and an additional six with [[Paul McCartney and Wings|Wings]]).{{cite magazine | url=https://www.billboard.com/artist/paul-mccartney/chart-history/hsi/ | title=Paul McCartney | Biography, Music & News | magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]] }} It also happened to be the number-one single in the US the week immediately preceding the induction of the Beatles into the [[Rock and Roll Hall of Fame]], making Harrison one of the few inductees to have an active single on the US record charts at the time of induction. ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' ranked the song as number three for 1988.[[Billboard Year-End Hot 100 singles of 1988]]. The single's B-side is "Lay His Head", a remixed version of an unreleased song originally intended for Harrison's ''[[Somewhere in England]]'' album. The [[twelve-inch single|twelve-inch version]] of the single also adds an extended version of "Got My Mind Set on You". In the UK, it was released on October 16,{{cite book | last=Badman | first=Keith | title=The Beatles After the Breakup 1970-2000: A day-by-day diary | year=2001 | publisher=Omnibus Press | location=London | isbn=0-7119-7520-5 }} and spent four weeks at number two. It became the fifth best selling single of 1987. The song was included in the Harrison compilation albums ''[[Best of Dark Horse 1976–1989]]'' (1989) and ''[[Let It Roll: Songs by George Harrison]]'' (2009). A live version was recorded for his ''[[Live in Japan (George Harrison album)|Live in Japan]]'' (1992) album. In 2010, AOL radio listeners chose "Got My Mind Set on You" as one of the ''10 Best George Harrison Songs'', appearing at number four on the list.{{cite web |url=http://www.aolradioblog.com/2010/04/03/best-george-harrison-songs/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100405020045/http://www.aolradioblog.com/2010/04/03/best-george-harrison-songs/ |url-status=usurped |archive-date=April 5, 2010 |author=Scott Shetler |title=10 Best George Harrison Songs |website=AOL Radio Blog |date=}}

It was released on October 12, 1987, in the US. Of Harrison's three number-one singles in the US, it was the only song not written or composed by Harrison himself. Not only was it the last US number-one hit by Harrison but, {{As of|2026|lc=y}}, the last time a former Beatle hit number one in either the US or UK as a solo artist. Billboard ranked the song as number three for 1988. The single's B-side is "Lay His Head", a remixed version of an unreleased song originally intended for Harrison's Somewhere in England album. The twelve-inch version of the single also adds an extended version of "Got My Mind Set on You". In the UK, it was released on October 16, and spent four weeks at number two. It became the fifth best selling single of 1987. The song was included in the Harrison compilation albums Best of Dark Horse 1976–1989 (1989) and Let It Roll: Songs by George Harrison (2009). A live version was recorded for his Live in Japan (1992) album. sections.wikitext:
Two [[music video]]s were released for the single. The first was directed by Willy Smax<ref>{{Cite web |title=George Harrison September 1987: Got My Mind Set On You #1A |url=https://beatlesonfilm.com/gh19870901a.html}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=George Harrison: Got My Mind Set on You (Version 1) [MV] |url=https://mubi.com/en/us/films/george-harrison-got-my-mind-set-on-you-mv}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=George Harrison - Got My Mind Set On You [Single/Album Version] |url=https://www.jefflynnesongs.com/popup.php?data=GotMyMindSetOnYou198717_popupplus}}</ref>, the second by [[Gary Weis]]. The first features a young man (played by [[Alexis Denisof]]) trying to win the heart of a girl in an [[amusement arcade]]. While the girl watches Harrison and his band (including [[Jeff Lynne]] on bass and [[Ray Cooper]] miming the saxophone) in a [[kinetoscope]] movie viewer, the young man tries to win a toy ballerina for the girl. He succeeds, but the ballerina somehow drops into Harrison's performance, to the girl's amusement.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.mvdbase.com/video.php?id=12647 |title=George Harrison – "Got My Mind Set on You [version 1: nickelodeon]" |publisher=mvdbase.com |access-date=April 23, 2009 |archive-date=October 7, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121007235854/http://www.mvdbase.com/video.php?id=12647 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

The second video, inspired by the then-recently released [[comedy horror]] film ''[[Evil Dead II]]'', depicts Harrison playing a blonde-colored [[Fender Telecaster]] guitar while seated in a [[study (room)|study]].<ref name="mvdbase1">{{cite web |url=http://www.mvdbase.com/video.php?id=12648 |title=George Harrison – "Got my mind set on you [version 2: chair]" |publisher=mvdbase.com |access-date=April 23, 2009 |archive-date=October 7, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121007235859/http://www.mvdbase.com/video.php?id=12648 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite tweet |user=GeorgeHarrison |number=1375114904152154112 |date=March 25, 2021 |title=The music video for George's "Got My Mind Set on You" was a spoof of the 1987 horror comedy film, 'Evil Dead II' and was his third #1 single in the US... |link=https://twitter.com/georgeharrison/status/1375114904152154112 |access-date=January 5, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.stereogum.com/2143088/the-number-ones-george-harrisons-got-my-mind-set-on-you/columns/the-number-ones/ |title=The Number Ones: George Harrison's "Got My Mind Set On You" |last=Breihan |first=Tom |date=April 7, 2021 |website=[[Stereogum]] |access-date=January 5, 2022}}</ref> As the song progresses, furniture and knick-knacks (including a stuffed squirrel, sentient chainsaw, a suit of armor, and mounted stag and [[warthog]]) begin to sing or dance along with the song. During the instrumental break, Harrison performs a [[backflip]] from his chair and follows it with a dance routine before jumping back to his seat, a scene performed by a [[Double_(occupation)#Dance_double|dance double]]. The video was choreographed by [[Vincent Paterson]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.beatlesbible.com/people/george-harrison/songs/got-my-mind-set-on-you/ |title=Got My Mind Set On You|date=September 14, 2023 |website=The Beatles Bible}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://msaagency.com/wp-content/themes/msa_twentytwo/profile_pdf/vincent-paterson-3159.pdf |title=Vincent Paterson |website=msaagency.com |page=4 |access-date=November 4, 2023 |archive-date=December 17, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231217213208/https://msaagency.com/wp-content/themes/msa_twentytwo/profile_pdf/vincent-paterson-3159.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref>

The second video received significant airplay and was nominated for three [[MTV Video Music Awards]].<ref name="mvdbase1" />
sections.text:
Two music videos were released for the single. The first was directed by Willy Smax, the second by Gary Weis. The first features a young man (played by Alexis Denisof) trying to win the heart of a girl in an amusement arcade. While the girl watches Harrison and his band (including Jeff Lynne on bass and Ray Cooper miming the saxophone) in a kinetoscope movie viewer, the young man tries to win a toy ballerina for the girl. He succeeds, but the ballerina somehow drops into Harrison's performance, to the girl's amusement.

The second video, inspired by the then-recently released comedy horror film Evil Dead II, depicts Harrison playing a blonde-colored Fender Telecaster guitar while seated in a study. As the song progresses, furniture and knick-knacks (including a stuffed squirrel, sentient chainsaw, a suit of armor, and mounted stag and warthog) begin to sing or dance along with the song. During the instrumental break, Harrison performs a backflip from his chair and follows it with a dance routine before jumping back to his seat, a scene performed by a dance double. The video was choreographed by Vincent Paterson.

The second video received significant airplay and was nominated for three MTV Video Music Awards.

sections.heading: Certifications
Other covers and parodies
sections.wikitext:
[["Weird Al" Yankovic]] recorded a parody of "Got My Mind Set On You" using George Harrison's arrangement, titled "(This Song's Just) Six Words Long". It was released on Yankovic's 1988 album ''[[Even Worse]]''<ref>{{cite web |url=https://secondhandsongs.com/release/4523 |title=Even Worse by "Weird Al" Yankovic |website=SecondHandSongs |access-date=7 November 2024}}</ref> and poked fun at Harrison's repetitive lyrics.

[[Shakin' Stevens]] recorded the song for his 2006 album ''Now Listen''.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.allmusic.com/song/got-my-mind-set-on-you-mt0015967005 |title=Got My Mind Set on You by Shakin' Stevens|website=AllMusic |access-date=7 November 2024}}</ref> Irish-Australian singer-songwriter [[Damien Leith]] recorded the song in 2012 for his album ''[[Now & Then (Damien Leith album)|Now & Then]]''. Irish singer [[Lee Matthews (singer)|Lee Matthews]] covered it in his 2015 album ''It's a Great Day to Be Alive''. British entertainer and musician  Warren James performed the song following his 2003 live performance for the show business charity the [[Grand Order of Water Rats]], an organisation that Harrison was an active member of. [[Brandon Flowers]] recorded the song in 2014 for the 2016 tribute album ''[[George Fest]]''.
sections.text:
"Weird Al" Yankovic recorded a parody of "Got My Mind Set On You" using George Harrison's arrangement, titled "(This Song's Just) Six Words Long". It was released on Yankovic's 1988 album Even Worse and poked fun at Harrison's repetitive lyrics.

Shakin' Stevens recorded the song for his 2006 album Now Listen. Irish-Australian singer-songwriter Damien Leith recorded the song in 2012 for his album Now & Then. Irish singer Lee Matthews covered it in his 2015 album It's a Great Day to Be Alive. British entertainer and musician  Warren James performed the song following his 2003 live performance for the show business charity the Grand Order of Water Rats, an organisation that Harrison was an active member of. Brandon Flowers recorded the song in 2014 for the 2016 tribute album George Fest.
